launches.name: Long March 3B | TJS-2 (TJSW-2)
launches.mission_desc: This is supposedly a test communications satellite to operate in geostationary orbit.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Kuaizhou 1A | Multiple payloads
launches.mission_desc: Lingqiao (or known as Jilin 1) is a small remote sensing satellite designed to capture videos with a ground resolution of 1.3 m. This is a third satellite of the Lingqiao series.
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | Iridium-1
launches.mission_desc: SpaceXâ€™s Falcon 9 rocket will deliver 10 satellites to low Earth orbit for Iridium, a global leader in mobile voice and data satellite communications. This is the first set of 10 satellites in a series of 75 total satellites that SpaceX will launch for Iridiumâ€™s next generation global satellite constellation, IridiumÂ® NEXT.

launches.name: SS-520-4 | TRICOM-1
launches.mission_desc: TRICOM-1 is an experimental 3U cubsat build by University of Tokyo. It is equipped with 5 small cameras for Earth imaging purposes, and is also tasked with storing and transmitting data between ground terminals.

launches.name: Atlas V 401 | SBIRS GEO Flight 3 (SBIRS GEO-4)
launches.mission_desc: This geostationary satellite is tasked with providing capabilities for early missile warning and missile defense.

launches.name: H-IIA 204 | DSN 2 (Kirameki 2)
launches.mission_desc: DSN 2, also known as Kirameki 2, is a geostationary communications satellite to be used for military communications by the Japanese military.

launches.name: Soyuz STB/Fregat-MT | Hispasat 36W-1 (Hispasat AG1)
launches.mission_desc: Hispasat 36W-1, also known as Hispasat AG-1, is a Spanish geostationary communications satellite. Joining the Hispasat fleet, this 3200 kg satellite is to operate in orbit for 15 years, providing its multimedia services to Europe, the Canary Islands and South America.

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | SKY Brasil-1 (Intelsat-32e) & Telkom-3S
launches.mission_desc:
Sky Brasil-1 (also known as Intelsat 32e) is a geostationary satellite to provide direct-to-home broadcasting services over Brazil.
Telkom-3S is an Indonesian geostationary communications satellite. It is a replacement for Telkom-3, which was stranded in an unusable orbit due to launch failure in 2012.

launches.name: PSLV XL | Cartosat-2D & 103 others
launches.mission_desc: Cartosat 2D is a remote sensing satellite for ISRO and is tasked with land observation from sun-synchronous orbit. It is launched along with 103 small satellites of foreign companies and research groups. Among these, 88 cubesats are Earth-imaging Dove satellites operated by Planet Labs company.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre First Launch Pad

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | SpX CRS-10
launches.mission_desc: SpaceX launched the Dragon spacecraft on their tenth operational cargo delivery mission to the International Space Station. The flight was conducted under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

launches.name: Soyuz-U | Progress MS-05 (66P)
launches.mission_desc: The Progress resupply vehicle is an automated, unpiloted version of the Soyuz spacecraft that is used to bring supplies and fuel to the International Space Station.

launches.name: SpaceShipTwo | VSS Unity GF03
launches.mission_desc: Free glide test flight of VSS Unity.

launches.name: Atlas V 401 | NROL-79
launches.mission_desc: Classified payload for the National Reconnaissance Office.

launches.name: Kaituozhe-2 | Tiankun-1
launches.mission_desc: This is the maiden launch of Kaitouzhe-2 rocket. Tiankun-1 is a new technology test satellite developed and built by China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation and it will be launched into a Sun-synchronous orbit.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Vega | Sentinel-2B
launches.mission_desc: Sentinel-2 is the second mission for Europeâ€™s Copernicus environment monitoring programme. It's a satellite constellation of two identical spacecrafts, Sentinel-2A and -2B. Both carry an innovative wide swath high-resolution multispectral imager with 13 spectral bands for a new perspective of our land and vegetation.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | Echostar 23
launches.mission_desc: Echostar 23 is a geostationary communications satellite, which will provide direct-to-home television broadcast services over Brazil. Being a flexible Ku-band satellite, it is capable of providing service from any of eight different orbital slots.

launches.name: H-IIA 202 | IGS Radar 5
launches.mission_desc: IGS Radar is a family of Japanese radar reconnaissance satellites that serve both Japan's national defense and civil natural disaster monitoring. IGS Radar 5 is the fifth generation of satellites. Equipped with synthetic aperture radar, it is able to image targets even in darkness and bad weather.

launches.name: Delta IV M+(5,4) | WGS-9 (USA-275)
launches.mission_desc: WGS-9 is the ninth of 10 high-capacity military communications satellites providing vital service for tactical forces who rely on WGS for connectivity to the Defence Information Systems Network (DISN).

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | SES-10
launches.mission_desc:
SES-10 is a 5300 kg geostationary communications satellite, which will replace AMC 2 and AMC 3 satellites. It will provide coverage over Mexico, Central and South Americas, and the Caribbean.

The SES-10 mission will mark a historic milestone on the road to full and rapid reusability as the worldâ€™s first reflight of an orbital class rocket. Falcon 9â€™s first stage for the SES-10 mission previously supported the successful CRS-8 mission in April 2016.

launches.name: Long March 3B | Shijian-13/Chinasat-16
launches.mission_desc: This is a Chinese experimental geostationary communications satellite. Besides testing the electric propulsion, the satellite is also reported to carry Chinas first high-throughput satellite payload (HTS), with a capacity of 20 GB per second. The satellite is aiming to provide Ka-band satellite broadband and multimedia services. Additionally it is also to conduct space-to-ground laser communications experiments.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Atlas V 401 | Cygnus CRS OA-7 (S.S. John Glenn)
launches.mission_desc: This is the eighth planned flight of the Orbital ATK's unmanned resupply spacecraft Cygnus and its seventh flight to the International Space Station under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA. Orbital ATK named the vehicle after astronaut John Glenn, the first American to orbit Earth and pioneer of human spaceflight.

launches.name: Soyuz-FG | Soyuz MS-04
launches.mission_desc: Soyuz MS-04 begins expedition 51 by carrying NASA astronaut Jack Fischer and Roscosmos cosmonaut Fyodor Yurchikhin to the International Space Station. After launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, they will rendezvous to the station where they will remain for their 6 month stay.

launches.name: Long March 7 | Tianzhou-1
launches.mission_desc: Tianzhou 1 is the first Chinese uncrewed cargo spacecraft to service the Tiangong 2 and follow on space stations.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Wenchang Space Launch Site, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | NROL-76
launches.mission_desc: Classified payload for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office.

launches.name: SpaceShipTwo | VSS Unity GF04
launches.mission_desc: Free glide test flight of VSS Unity.

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | SGDC 1 & Koreasat 7
launches.mission_desc: Both SGDC 1 and Koreasat 7 are geostationary telecommunications satellites. SGDC 1 is a 5800 kg satellite for Brazil, equipped with 50 Ka-band and 7 X-band transponders, and intended for both civil and military use. Koreasat 7 is to provide internet access, multimedia, broadcasting and fixed communications services to South Korea, Philippines, Indonesia and India. Satellite weighs around 3500 kg, and its operational lifetime is 15 years.

launches.name: GSLV Mk II | SouthAsiaSat (GSAT-9)
launches.mission_desc: GSAT-9 is a multi band communication and observation satellite. It carries a GAGAN (regional Indian GPS navigational system) navigation payload to provide GPS services to security forces and air traffic control organizations. Weighing about 2330 kg, satellite has an operational lifetime of 12 years.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre Second Launch Pad

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | Inmarsat-5 F4
launches.mission_desc: Inmarsat-5 F4 is the next addition to the fifth generation of Inmarsat satellites. Inmarsat-5 satellites each carry 89 Ka-band beams and deliver high-speed mobile broadband communications for deep sea vessels, in-flight connectivity for airline passengers, streaming high-resolution video, voice and date to the enterprise sector, and secure solutions for government customers. The satellite weighs 6100 kg at launch and has an operational lifetime of 15 years.

launches.name: Soyuz STA/Fregat | SES-15
launches.mission_desc: SES 15 is a geostationary communications satellite operating in Ka- and Ku-bands in North America, which uses electric propulsion for initial orbit raising and all on-orbit manoeuvres.

launches.name: Electron | It's a Test
launches.mission_desc: This is the first test flight of the Electron rocket. Built and operated by Rocket Lab, Electron is meant to offer low-price launches for the small-sat market.
launches.location: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1, Mahia Peninsula, New Zealand
launches.fail_reason: Third-party contractor supporting the launch misconfigured ground equipment that translated radio signals from the rocket into data used by range safety officials. That caused â€œextensive corruption of received position data,â€ resulting in the data loss that led safety officials to trigger the rocketâ€™s flight termination system.

launches.name: Soyuz-2.1b/Fregat | EKS-2 (Tundra 2) (Kosmos 2518)
launches.mission_desc: The Tundra or EKS (meaning Unified Space System) series of satellites is the next generation of Russian early warning satellites.

launches.name: H-IIA 202 | Michibiki 2 (QZS-2)
launches.mission_desc: The Quasi-Zenith Satellite System (QZSS) is a three-satellite regional time transfer system and the satellite-based augmentation system for the GPS that would be receivable within Japan. The primary purpose of QZSS is to increase the availability of GPS in Japan's numerous urban canyons, where only satellites at very high elevation can be seen. A secondary function is performance enhancement, increasing the accuracy and reliability of GPS derived navigation solutions. A single satellite weighs about 4000 kg, has an expected lifetime of 15 years and is put in a elliptical, highly inclined geosynchronous orbit.

launches.name: SpaceShipTwo | VSS Unity CF01
launches.mission_desc: Cold flow test flight of VSS Unity.

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | ViaSat-2 & EUTELSAT 172B
launches.mission_desc:
ViaSat-2 is a commercial communications satellite with an estimated capacity of 350 Gbit/s. The satellite will provide satellite internet to North America, parts of South America, the Caribbean, and the Atlantic Ocean.
Eutelsat 172B is a communications satellite featuring a C-band, a Ku-band and a high throughput payload and all electric orbital raising. It is to reside in 172Â° East, where it will provide coverage of the Asia-Pacific.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | SpX CRS-11
launches.mission_desc: SpaceX launched the Dragon spacecraft on their eleventh operational cargo delivery mission to the International Space Station. The flight was conducted under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA. This is the first reflight of a reused Dragon spacecraft. This Dragon capsule first flew on CRS-4.

launches.name: LVM-3 | GSAT-19
launches.mission_desc: GSAT-19 is an Indian geostationary communications satellite. With a mass of 3200 kg and expected operational lifetime of 15 years, this satellite will test several epxerimental technologies like electrical propulsion, deployable thermal radiatiors, indigenious Li-Ion batteries.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre Second Launch Pad

launches.name: Proton-M Briz-M | Echostar 21
launches.mission_desc: Echostar 21, formerly known as TerreStar 2, is a geostationary communications satellite built by Space System/Loral company. Equipped with S-band transponders, satellite is tasked with providing mobile broadband services over Europe. The spacecraft, based on SSLâ€™s 1300 bus, will be located at the 10.25Â° East orbital slot.

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1a | Progress MS-06 (67P)
launches.mission_desc: The Progress resupply vehicle is an automated, unpiloted version of the Soyuz spacecraft that is used to bring supplies and fuel to the International Space Station.

launches.name: Long March 4B | Huiyan (HXMT (Hard X-ray Modulation Telescope))
launches.mission_desc: Hard X-ray Modulation Telescope (HXMT) is a Chinese X-ray space observatory. This will be China's first astronomy satellite, and it is tasked with observation of black holes, neutron stars and other phenomena based on their X-ray and gamma ray emissions.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Long March 3B/E | Zhongxing-9A (Chinasat-9A)
launches.mission_desc: ChinaSat-9A is based on the DFH-4 satellite platform and is to provide direct broadcast services with eighteen 36MHz and four 54MHz BSS Ku band transponders. Together with ChinaSat-9 direct broadcast satellite, ChinaSat 9A is designed to serve the radio and TV transmission, digital film and digital broadband multi-media system as well as information and entertainment broadcasting market.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China
launches.fail_reason: The satellite was placed into the wrong orbit due to a third stage anomaly. However, the payload recovered using onboard propulsion.

launches.name: PSLV XL | Cartosat-2E
launches.mission_desc: Cartosat-2E is seventh of Cartosat series of Earth observation satellites to be deployed in 500 km sun-synchronous orbit. Its main purpose is to collect high resolution large-scale maps which will be used for urban planning, infrastructure development, utilities planning and traffic management.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre First Launch Pad

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1v/Volga | Kosmos-2519
launches.mission_desc: This is a payload for the Russian Ministry of Defense. According to officials, it is intended for Earth imaging and imaging of space objects purposes.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | BulgariaSat-1
launches.mission_desc: BulgariaSat-1 is a geostationary communications satellite operated by Bulgaria Sat and manufactured by SSL. Its payload is composed of 30 Ku band BSS transponders and 2 Ku-band FSS transponders for fixed satellite services and high-definition television broadcasts. It is designed to deliver service for 15 years with a projected fuel life of over 20 years. BulgariaSat-1 is designed to provide direct-to-home television service and data communications services to the Balkans and other European regions.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | Iridium-2
launches.mission_desc: SpaceXâ€™s Falcon 9 rocket will deliver 10 satellites to low Earth orbit for Iridium, a global leader in mobile voice and data satellite communications. This is the second set of 10 satellites in a series of 75 total satellites that SpaceX will launch for Iridiumâ€™s next generation global satellite constellation, IridiumÂ® NEXT.

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | Hellas Sat 3 (Inmarsat S EAN) & GSAT-17
launches.mission_desc: Hellas-Sat 3 is a powerful telecommunications condominium satellite for Inmarsat and Hellas-Sat. The satellite will provide Mobile Satellite Services (MSS), Fixed Satellite Services (FSS) and Broadcast Satellite Services (BSS). It is equipped with Ka/S-band payload, 47 Ku-band transponders, 1 Ka-band transponder. Weighing 5900 kg at launch, the satellite is to reside in geostationary orbit in an orbital position 39Â° East, where it is expected to operate for about 15 years. GSAT-17 is a communication satellite with a lift off mass of 3425 kg and 6 KW power generation capacity. The satellite's commercial transponders include Ku-band, Normal C-band and Extended C-band transponders. It additionally carries a dedicated transponder for data relay (DRT) and search-and-rescue (SAR) services.

launches.name: Long March 5 / YZ-2 | Shijian 18
launches.mission_desc: Shijian 18 is a Chinese experimental geostationary satellite based on the new DFH-5 Bus. Reportedly the transmission capacity of the satellite is double that of current Chinese communications satellites, allowing more television channels and clearer programs to be transmitted. The new satellite will also improve internet connectivity and accessibility as well as reduce users' costs.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Wenchang Space Launch Site, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | Intelsat 35e
launches.mission_desc: Intelsat 35e is a geostationary communications satellite for Intelsat. It is the fourth satellite of the EpicNG service, and will cover the Americas, Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa from the 34.5Â°West orbital position.

launches.name: Soyuz-2.1a/Fregat | Kanopus-V-IK
launches.mission_desc: Kanopus-V-IK is a small Russian remote sensing satellite for monitoring wildfires. Weighing about 473 kg, it is intended for 5 years of operation in a 510 km sun-synchronous orbit.
launches.fail_reason: Numerous payloads experienced technical problems after an upper stage anomaly.

launches.name: Simorgh | Unknown
launches.mission_desc: First test flight of the Simorgh rocket, intended to reach orbit. Pentagon officials confirmed the launch occurred at around 9:30 UTC on Thursday and did not place a satellite in orbit.
launches.location: Semnan Space Center, Islamic Republic of Iran
launches.fail_reason: Failure due to a problem with the second stage, which failed after 20 seconds of powered flight (of planned 300 seconds).

launches.name: Soyuz-FG | Soyuz MS-05
launches.mission_desc: Soyuz MS-05 begins expedition 52 by carrying NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA astronaut Paolo Nespoli and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Ryazansky to the International Space Station. After launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, they will rendezvous to the station where they will remain for their 6 month stay.

launches.name: MOMO | 1st Test Flight
launches.mission_desc:
First Test Flight of the MOMO suborbital rocket.
Flight was terminated about 80 seconds after engine ignition.
launches.fail_reason: Flight was terminated about 80 seconds after engine ignition.

launches.name: Vega | OptSat 3000 & VENÂµS (VENUS)
launches.mission_desc: OptSat 3000 is an Earth imaging satellite built by Israel Aerospace Industries for the Italian military. It will be placed in a sun-synchronous orbit at an altitude of 600km. It will have a mission life of more than six years. Launched along with it is VENÂµS, Vegetation and Environment monitoring on a New Micro-Satellite. This is a near polar sun-synchronous orbit microsatellite jointly built by the Israeli Space Agency and CNES. Besides the scientific mission of terrestrial environment monitoring, the satellite is also tasked with verification and validation of the Hall Effect thruster in space.

launches.name: SpaceShipTwo | VSS Unity GF06
launches.mission_desc: Free glide test flight of VSS Unity.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | SpX CRS-12
launches.mission_desc: SpaceX launched the Dragon spacecraft on their 12th operational cargo delivery mission to the International Space Station. The flight was conducted under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

launches.name: Proton-M/Briz-M | Blagovest No.11L (Kosmos 2520)
launches.mission_desc: This is a military communications satellite developed for the Russian Defence Ministry. Blagovest â„–11L is fitted with Ku-band and Q-band transponders and is expected to operate in geostationary orbit for 15 years.
launches.lsp: Khrunichev State Research and Production Space Center

launches.name: Atlas V 401 | TDRS-M
launches.mission_desc: TDRS-M is an American communications satellite which is operated by NASA as part of the Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System, which provides a multitude of communications services to a wide variety of missions.

launches.name: H-IIA 204 | Michibiki 3 (QZS-3)
launches.mission_desc: The Quasi-Zenith Satellite System (QZSS) is a three-satellite regional time transfer system and the satellite-based augmentation system for the GPS that would be receivable within Japan. The primary purpose of QZSS is to increase the availability of GPS in Japan's numerous urban canyons, where only satellites at very high elevation can be seen. A secondary function is performance enhancement, increasing the accuracy and reliability of GPS derived navigation solutions. A single satellite weighs about 4000 kg, has an expected lifetime of 15 years and is put in a elliptical, highly inclined geosynchronous orbit.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | Formosat 5
launches.mission_desc: Formosat 5 is an Earth observation satellite developed by the Taiwan's National Space Organization (NSPO). Weighing about 475 kg, it will reside in a sun-synchronous orbit at 720-km altitude.

launches.name: Minotaur IV | ORS-5
launches.mission_desc: Also known as SensorSat, the Operationally Responsive Space 5 (ORS-5) will perform surveillance on geostationary (GEO) satellites. The craft will provide a stopgap for the existing space based surveillance system (SBSS), since full replacements are not expected until after 2020. With a mass of approximately 100kg the solar powered craft will operate in low earth orbit at an altitude of 600km.

launches.name: PSLV XL | IRNSS-1H
launches.mission_desc: This is a replacement satellite for the IRNSS-1A of the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System. The constellation will provide India with an alternative to GPS and will be used for military and civilian use. Located at a geosynchronous orbit the system will be operated by the Indian government.
launches.pad: Satish Dhawan Space Centre First Launch Pad

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | OTV-5 (X-37B)
launches.mission_desc: It is the fifth flight of the X-37B program. United States Air Force Orbital Test Vehicle, built by Boeing, is an unmanned 5000 kg, 8.8 m-long reusable mini-spaceplane capable of autonomous re-entry and landing.

launches.name: Proton-M Briz-M | Amazonas 5
launches.mission_desc: Amazonas 5 is a spanish geostationary communications satellite for Hispasat. It is a replacement for the Amazonas 4A satellite and provides coverage for Brazil and Latin America. Satellite carries 24 Ku-band transponders and 35 Ka-band spot beams, and has an operational lifetime of 15 years.

launches.name: Soyuz-FG | Soyuz MS-06
launches.mission_desc: Soyuz MS-06 begins expedition 53 by carrying NASA astronauts Mark Vande Hei, Joseph Acaba and Roscosmos cosmonaut Alexander Misurkin to the International Space Station. After launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, they will rendezvous to the station where they will remain for their 6 month stay.

launches.name: Soyuz-2.1b/Fregat-M | Glonass-M (Kosmos 2522)
launches.mission_desc: Glonass-M, also known as Uragan-M, are the second generation of Uragan satellite design used for GLONASS satellite navigation system. GLONASS is a Russian space-based navigation system comparable to the similar GPS and Galileo systems. This generation improves on accuracy, power consumption and design life. Each satellite weighs 1415 kg, is equipped with 12 L-band antennas, and has an operational lifetime of 7 years.

launches.name: Atlas V 541 | NROL-42
launches.mission_desc: Classified payload for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office.

launches.name: Proton-M Briz-M | AsiaSat 9
launches.mission_desc: AsiaSat 9 is AsiaSatâ€™s next generation satellite to replace AsiaSat 4 at 122 degrees East Longitude. AsiaSat 9 is a Space Systems/Loral 1300E satellite equipped with 28 C-band and 32 Ku-band transponders, and a Ka-band payload. AsiaSat 9 will provide additional capacity, enhanced power and coverage for DTH, video distribution, private networks and broadband services across the Asia-Pacific region.

launches.name: Long March 2C | 3 x Yaogan-30-01
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Ariane 5 ECA | Intelsat 37e & BSAT-4a
launches.mission_desc:
Intelsat 37e is a geostationary communications satellite for Intelsat, another one of the EpicNG series. It weighs about 6700 kg and is equipped with C-band, Ku-band and Ka-band transopnders. Intelsat 37e is a replacement for the Intelsat 901 spacecraft in the 18Â° W orbital slot, covering Europe, Africa, South America and North America. 
BSAT-4a is a geostationary communications satellite for the Japanese satellite operator B-SAT. Satellite is equipped with 24 Ku transponders and weighs about 3500 kg. It is to reside in 110Â° East orbital position, providing high-resolution direct television broadcasting to Japan.

launches.name: Long March 2D | VRSS-2 (Antonio JosÃ© de Sucre)
launches.mission_desc: VRSS-2 is the second Venezuelan remote sensing satellite. Spacecraft was built by China. Weighing about 1000 kg, it is to operate in sun-synchronous orbit at an altitude of 645 kilometres, providing services in traffic management, disaster warning and prevention, tracking agriculture and land use.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.mission_desc:
SpaceXâ€™s Falcon 9 rocket will deliver 10 satellites to low Earth
orbit for Iridium, a global leader in mobile voice and
data satellite communications. This is the third set of 10
satellites in a series of 75 total satellites that SpaceX will

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | Echostar 105/SES-11
launches.mission_desc: Echostar 105, also known as SES-11, is a partnership between Echostar and SES for a communications satellite at the orbital position of 105 degrees West. Satellite's Ku-band and C-band capacity will allow it to replace the AMC-15 and AMC-18 satellites. Echostar 105 is to provide coverage of the North America, including Hawaii, Mexico, the Caribbean.

launches.name: Rokot / Briz-KM | Sentinel-5P
launches.mission_desc: Sentinel-5P, also known as Sentinel-5 Precursor, is an Earth observation satellite developed by European space agency as a part of Copernicus Programme. Being the first mission of the program dedicated to monitoring air pollution, Sentinel-5P is tasked to perform atmospheric measurements relating to air quality, climate forcing, ozone and UV radiation.

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1a | Progress MS-07 (68P)
launches.mission_desc: The Progress resupply vehicle is an automated, unpiloted version of the Soyuz spacecraft that is used to bring supplies and fuel to the International Space Station.

launches.name: Atlas V 421 | NROL-52
launches.mission_desc: Classified payload for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Block 4 | Koreasat 5A
launches.mission_desc: Koreasat 5A is a telecommunitations satellite to provide internet access, fixed telecommunications, media and broadcasting services. Loaded with Ku-band transponders, this satellite will cover Korea, Japan, Indochina and Middle East.

launches.name: Minotaur-C (Taurus XL) | 6 x SkySat & 4 x Dove
launches.mission_desc: Dedicated rideshare

launches.name: Long March 3B / YZ-1 | Beidou-3 M1 & M2
launches.mission_desc: The BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) is a Chinese satellite navigation system. It consists of two separate satellite constellations â€“ a limited test system that has been operating since 2000, and a full-scale global navigation system that is currently under construction. Two Beidou Navigation Satellite will be launched atop of a Long March 3B (CZ-3B) from Xichang Satellite Launch Center to medium Earth orbit.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Vega | Mohammed VI-A
launches.mission_desc: An Earth observation satellite for the Kingdom of Morocco. It was developed by Thales Alenia Space and Airbus. Satellite will be in particular used for mapping and land surveying activities, regional development, agricultural monitoring, the prevention and management of natural disasters, monitoring changes in the environment and desertification, as well as border and coastal surveillance.

launches.name: Antares 230 | Cygnus CRS OA-8 (S.S. Gene Cernan)
launches.mission_desc: This is the ninth planned flight of the Orbital ATK's unmanned resupply spacecraft Cygnus and its eighth flight to the International Space Station under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

launches.name: Long March 4C | Fengyun-3D
launches.mission_desc: Fengyun-3D (also known as FY-3D) is a polar orbiting meteorological satellite. It is tasked with ocean and ice monitoring, as well as studying atmospheric chemistry and space weather. The satellite is expected to operate for 5 years.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Delta II 7920-10 | JPSS 1 (Joint Polar Satellite System spacecraft No. 1)
launches.mission: JPSS 1 (Joint Polar Satellite System spacecraft No. 1)
launches.mission_desc: From a 512-mile orbit, tilted 98.7 degrees to the equator and traveling pole-to-pole, the craft will provide imagery, atmospheric temperature and humidity profiles, and land and ocean surface temperature observations, all of which are key ingredients for weather forecasting. In addition, the satellite will measure ozone levels and reflected solar radiation from the planet.JPSS 1 will survey the entire globe twice per day with five sensor packages.The satellite will replace the existing Suomi NPP spacecraft that launched in 2011 for a five-year mission as a gapfiller between NOAAâ€™s legacy weather satellite constellation and the new JPSS generation.

launches.name: Long March 6 | Jilin-1-04, Jilin-1-05 & Jilin-1-06
launches.mission_desc: Jilin-1 is a series of Chinese commercial remote sensing satellites.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Long March 2C | 3 x Yaogan-30
launches.mission_desc: The Yaogan-30 is a series of military remote sensing satellites which are launched in triplets. The satellites are spaced by 120° in their orbit.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Soyuz 2.1b/Fregat | Meteor-M No.2-1 & rideshare payloads
launches.mission_desc: This is the third spacecraft in the Russian Meteor-M series of remote sensing satellites. Weighing about 2750 kg, it is intended to gather hydrometeorological data from sun-synchronous orbit. This includes monitoring ozone layer and radiation levels in the near-Earth space, as well as monitoring ocean surface temperatures and ice conditions.
launches.fail_reason: An algorithm glitch caused the Fregat upper stage to de-orbit.

launches.name: Soyuz-2.1b | Lotos-S1 (Kosmos-2524)
launches.mission_desc: Lotos-S1 spacecraft is a part of the Liana constellation, designed for orbital electronic intelligence.

launches.name: Long March 2D | LKW-1 (Land Survey Satellite-1)
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: Long March 3B/E | Alcomsat-1
launches.mission_desc: Alcomsat-1 is the first Algerian telecommunications satellite. It is expected to operate in geostationary orbit for 15 years. Satellite carries Ku-band and Ka-band transponders for civil applications and X-band, UHF and EHF for the needs of the military and strategic state sectors.
launches.lsp: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
launches.location: Xichang Satellite Launch Center, People's Republic of China

launches.name: New Shepard | NS-7
launches.mission_desc: NS-7 is Blue Origins first commercial flight. The payloads included 12 experiments conducted in 3 minutes of microgravity dedicated to medical and earth science.
launches.pad: West Texas Suborbital Launch Site/ Corn Ranch
launches.location: Corn Ranch, Van Horn, TX, USA

launches.name: Ariane 5 ES | Galileo L9 (FOC FM15-FM18)
launches.mission_desc: The Galileo constellation is ESA's satellite navigation system and is expected to be completed by 2020. Galileo will provide Europe with an alternative to the American GPS and Russian GLONASS constellations, but will be interoperable with both systems.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | SpX CRS-13
launches.mission_desc: SpaceX launched the Dragon spacecraft on their 13th operational cargo delivery mission to the International Space Station. The flight was conducted under the Commercial Resupply Services contract with NASA.

launches.name: Soyuz-FG | Soyuz MS-07
launches.mission_desc: Soyuz MS-07 begins expedition 54 by carrying NASA astronaut Scott Tingle, JAXA astronaut Norishige Kanai and Roscosmos cosmonaut Aleksander Skvortsov to the International Space Station. After launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, they will rendezvous to the station where they will remain for their 6 month stay.

launches.name: H-IIA 202 | GCOM-C1 & SLATS
launches.mission_desc: GCOM-C1 is another satellite in JAXA's Earth observation Global Change Observation Mission (GCOM) constellation. This spacecraft is the first satellite in GCOM-C series and is intended to operate in sun-synchronous orbit for 5 years. It aims to collect surface and atmospheric measurements in order to monitor global climate change. Along with it is launched an engineering test satellite SLATS (Super Low Altitude Test Satellite), which is an attempt to develop techniques to operate a satellite in extremely low orbits. SLATS will try achieve that by maintaining position in orbit via ion engines. It will also collect data on atmosphere density and measure atomic oxygen in such low altitudes.

launches.name: Falcon 9 Full Thrust | Iridium-4
launches.mission_desc: SpaceXâ€™s Falcon 9 rocket will deliver 10 satellites to low Earth orbit for Iridium, a global leader in mobile voice and data satellite communications. This is the fourth set of 10 satellites in a series of 75 total satellites that SpaceX will launch for Iridiumâ€™s next generation global satellite constellation, IridiumÂ® NEXT.

launches.name: Zenit-3F | AngoSat-1
launches.mission_desc: AngoSat-1 is a geostationary communications satellite operated by Angosat and built by Russian RSC Energia. It is Angola's first communications satellite. Angosat-1 is fitted with C-band and Ku-band transponders and has an operational lifetime of 15 years.
